speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any changes in your urinary habits, such as difficulty urinating or frequent need to urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That abdominal mass is pressing on your organs; besides the urinary issues we just discussed, have you noticed any bloating, early satiety, or pelvic pain? Also, has there been any change in bowel movements, such as constipation or a feeling of incomplete evacuation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Carcinoma with malignant ascites and pleural effusion.

The combination of a large ovarian mass, increased abdominal girth, shortness of breath, and fatigue without weight loss is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian cancer causing fluid accumulation. I am requesting a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to visualize the mass extent and ascites, along with a Thoracentesis to confirm pleural effusion.
